320955.title: Local induced-cycle conjecture for vertex-prescribed deletion
320955.literal_statement:
A graph is **$r$-connected** if deleting fewer than $r$ vertices leaves it connected. An induced cycle is a cycle with no edges between nonconsecutive cycle vertices.

**Vertex-prescribed induced-cycle conjecture.** For every $k$, there exists an $h(k)$ such that for every vertex $v$ of every $h(k)$-connected graph $G$, there exists an induced cycle $C$ containing $v$ such that $G-V(C)$ is $k$-connected.

This is a weaker local form of the high-connectivity-keeping cycle problem, while the corresponding edge-prescribed form is equivalent to the high-connectivity-keeping path conjecture. The source states that this problem is open.

318486.title: Symmetric product-state conjecture for maximal overlap of permutation-invariant states
318486.literal_statement: Let a permutation-invariant multipartite state be given, and consider its maximal overlap with product states. The question concerns whether the product state attaining this maximal overlap can be chosen with identical single-party factors. **Symmetric product-state conjecture.** Is it true that, in order to obtain the maximal overlap of any permutation-invariant state, we can assume the product state to be a tensor product of the same single-party state? The question asks whether optimization over arbitrary product states can always be reduced to optimization over symmetric product states. The supplied context says that only a partial answer follows, so the general claim is not established here.

322704.title: The ordinal Ramsey bound conjecture for well-founded trees
322704.literal_statement: A **well-founded tree** is a prefix-closed set of finite sequences, and its order type is the ordinal order type used in the paper. A coloring of such a tree assigns each node one of two colors, red or black. **Ordinal Ramsey bound conjecture.** There is a reasonably simple ordinal-valued binary partial function $F$ such that, for all ordinals $\beta$ and $\gamma$, some ordinal $\alpha\leq F(\beta,\gamma)$ has the property that every red-and-black coloring of every well-founded tree $T_0$ of order type $\alpha$ contains either a well-founded tree $T_1$ of order type $\beta$ homeomorphically embedded into the red nodes of $T_0$, or a well-founded tree $T_2$ of order type $\gamma$ homeomorphically embedded into the black nodes of $T_0$. This is posed to generalize the finite-order-type Ramsey bounds established earlier in the appendix; no resolution is given.

376778.title: Absence of pure point spectrum under dynamical avoidance
376778.literal_statement:
Let $d_\infty$ and $N$ be the parameters in the spectral construction, let $\phi$ be the associated map, let $g$ be the associated rational map, and let $I_{g^n}$ denote the indeterminacy points of $g^n$. For every real $\lambda$, assume there are open subsets $U\subset\mathbb C$ and $V\subset\mathbb L^G$ such that

$$
\lambda\in U,\qquad \bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty} I_{g^n}\subset V,\qquad g^n(\phi(U))\cap V=\emptyset.
$$

**Pure point spectrum conjecture.** If $d_\infty=N$ and this condition holds for every real $\lambda$, then

$$
\Sigma_{pp}=\emptyset.
$$

The question arises because the non-deterministic spectrum is related to the indeterminacy points of $g$, while pure point spectrum beyond the non-deterministic component would suggest that iterates of $g$ approach those points. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

388681.title: Rolling a Die over a Labeled Board
388681.literal_statement: Label the faces of a unit cube with numbers $1$--$6$ as in a die. Place the cube to sit on an integer lattice grid, with one corner at the origin and sides aligned with the axes. Completely label every lattice square of a rectangular ``board'' $R$, whose corner is at the origin, with numbers in $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$. The problem is to roll the cube over its edges so that, for each square $s \in B$ labeled $l$, the cube lands on $s$ precisely once, and when it does so, the top face of the cube has label $l$. What is the computational complexity of solving an instance of this problem?

388673.title: Monochromatic Triangles
388673.literal_statement: For any (planar) triangle $T$, is there is a $3$-coloring of the (infinite) plane with no monochromatic copy of $T$? We imagine congruent copies of $T$ moved around the plane via rigid motions, and seek a spot where $T$ is monochromatic. $T$ is monochromatic if its three vertices are painted the same color, by virtue of lying on points of the plane painted that color. Note that the coloring in the question may depend on the given triangle $T$.

320192.title: Bounded-endvertex path-packing conjecture for degenerate graphs
320192.literal_statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $G$ be a graph of degeneracy $d$, and let $c_k$ denote a constant depending on $k$. A collection of paths is **edge-disjoint** if no two paths share an edge, and it is **maximal** if no further path of the specified length can be added while preserving edge-disjointness. **Bounded-endvertex path-packing conjecture.** There is a maximal collection $\mathcal{C}$ of edge-disjoint paths of length $2k$ in $G$ such that every vertex of $G$ is an endvertex of at most $c_kd$ paths in $\mathcal{C}$. This is presented as an open question motivated by a proposition in the paper.

379937.title: Existence of sets with prescribed numbers of missing sums and differences
379937.literal_statement:
Let $j$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers with $k$ even. **Prescribed-defect existence conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $n$ and a set $S\subset\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ such that $0\in S$, $n-1\in S$, and

$$
|S+S|=2n-1-j,\qquad |S-S|=2n-1-k.
$$

This is posed as an open problem motivated by the preceding limiting-distribution conjecture. The source notes that Hegarty's methods establish it when $j\ge k/2$, while the general case remains open there.

359676.title: Herzog–Qureshi's equality conjecture for polymatroidal ideals
359676.literal_statement:
Let $I$ be a polymatroidal ideal. Write $\astab(I)$ for the index of stability of the associated-prime sets of the powers of $I$, and $\dstab(I)$ for the index of stability of their depth functions.

**Herzog–Qureshi's conjecture.** Does

$$
\astab(I)=\dstab(I)
$$

hold for every polymatroidal ideal $I$?

This asks whether the stabilization index of the associated primes always equals the stabilization index of the depth function for powers of a polymatroidal ideal. The supplied context attributes the question to Herzog and Qureshi but gives no evidence of a resolution, so its status is open.

351630.title: Weak-domination conjecture for reflective tree decompositions
351630.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected non-trivial bigraph, and let $T$ be a **reflective tree decomposition** of $G$ with core $H$. For each edge $\{U_1,U_2\}\in E(T)$, assume that $H$ weakly dominates $G\vert_{U_1\cap U_2}$. For every non-empty $V\subseteq V(T)$, **the weak-domination conjecture** asserts that $G$ weakly dominates

$$
G\vert_{\bigcup_{U\in V}U}.
$$

This is proposed as a natural generalization of a previously proved result on reflective tree decompositions and as a stepping stone toward replacing the forest restriction in higher-order decompositions by a weak-domination condition. The supplied text presents it as an open problem, and gives no resolution.

334042.title: Van Kampen obstruction criterion for simplicial maps of trees
334042.literal_statement:
Let $K$ be a tree and let $\varphi:K\to\mathbb R^2$ be a simplicial map. The van Kampen obstruction $v(\varphi)$ is the mod-$2$ obstruction defined from intersections of images of disjoint simplices; for polygonal lines, its vanishing is equivalent to approximability by embeddings.

**Van Kampen obstruction conjecture.** The van Kampen obstruction vanishes if and only if $\varphi$ is approximable by embeddings.

The corresponding equivalence is known for polygonal lines and is false for closed polygonal lines, including the standard $3$-winding. The question for simplicial maps of arbitrary trees is attributed to R. Skopenkov and Skopenkov's cited source, and remains unresolved in the supplied text.

317034.title: Universality of the polymatroid quasi-symmetric invariant
317034.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname{PolyMat}$ be the vector space of polymatroids, let $\operatorname{QSym}$ be the quasi-symmetric-function space, and let ${\mathcal G}:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to\operatorname{QSym}$ be the valuative invariant in the preceding theorem. A map $f:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to V$ is **valuative** when it preserves every rational linear relation among polymatroid base polytopes. **Universality conjecture.** For every $\mathbb{Q}$-linear valuative map $f:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to V$, there should exist a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map $\psi:\operatorname{QSym}\to V$ such that

$$
\psi\circ {\mathcal G}=f.
$$

This asks whether every valuative invariant factors through ${\mathcal G}$; the supplied text does not establish whether this universal property holds.

369524.title: The commutativity conjecture for excedance–antiexcedance elements
369524.literal_statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ be its group algebra. For a permutation $w\in S_n$, write $\operatorname{exc}w$ for the number of $i\in[n]$ such that $w(i)>i$, and $\operatorname{anxc}w$ for the number of $i\in[n]$ such that $w(i)<i$. For $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$, define

$$
\mathbf{X}_{a,b}:=\sumnonlimits\limits_{\substack{w\in S_n;\\operatorname{exc}w=a;\\operatorname{anxc}w=b}}w\in\mathbf{k}[S_n].
$$

**Commutativity conjecture.** For fixed $n$, the elements $\mathbf{X}_{a,b}$ commute for all $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$; equivalently,

$$
\mathbf{X}_{a,b}\mathbf{X}_{c,d}=\mathbf{X}_{c,d}\mathbf{X}_{a,b}
$$

for all $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{N}$. This is presented as an open problem concerning a family of combinatorially defined elements in the symmetric group algebra; the excerpt gives no evidence of a resolution.

365142.title: Efficient cleaning sequence for directed graphs
365142.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a directed graph, and consider cleaning sequences in which multiple vertices that are ready to fire may fire simultaneously. **Efficient-cleaning-sequence problem.** Determine the cleaning sequence that minimises both the number of brushes used and the time taken to clean $G$.

The brushing process involves deploying brushes to clean the arcs of a directed graph, with vertices firing when they are ready; allowing simultaneous firing introduces a time objective in addition to the brushing-number objective. It remains open to determine the most efficient such sequence in general.

345448.title: The convex-polytope realization question for convex codes
345448.literal_statement:
A **code** is a collection of subsets of a finite ground set. A code is **convex** if it has a realization by convex sets, and it is realized with **convex polytopes** if those realizing sets can be chosen to be convex polytopes.

**Convex-polytope realization question.** Can every convex code be realized with convex polytopes?

An affirmative answer would strengthen the paper's characterization of polytope-convex codes and could help determine whether convex-code recognition is algorithmically decidable. The source presents this as an open question; its resolution would be a first step toward resolving the convex code decision problem.
